column3: It directly names Satan as a manifest enemy and shows his work as obstructing the path.
It links an answered call to steadfastness and refusing an ignorant path, a useful contrast to Satan's call.
It adds Satan's deceptive whispering as a concrete means of drawing people away from God's command.
It directly joins Satan's manifest enmity with the command not to serve him.
The immediate sequel contrasts the severe punishment of disbelief with forgiveness and great reward for faith and good works.
It supplies a general precedent of disbelievers being given respite and then seized.
It shows Satan exploiting speech between people to create conflict, specifying one mode of his enmity.
It supplies the positive side of recompense for believers and good works, without the Satanic call.
It identifies several former peoples collectively as hostile parties, clarifying the social force of hizb.
It explicitly names Satan's party and connects his domination to forgetfulness of God and loss.
The preceding ayah warns that worldly life and the deceiver can mislead people about God.
It connects turning people away with Jahannam as blazing fire, strengthening the consequence side.
It states that whoever takes the deceiver as patron is led astray and guided toward the blazing fire.
It gives a general warning that wrongdoers face punishment beyond their awareness.
It portrays Satanic private counsel as a deliberate attempt to grieve believers.
It identifies Satan's use of fear through his allies and directs believers to fear God instead.
It concerns God's exclusive power to open or withhold mercy, without a direct enemy, call, or party relation.
It joins being astray with the fires, but does not specify Satan's recruiting activity.
It warns against taking Iblis and his offspring as patrons even though they are enemies, directly clarifying rival allegiance.
It presents refusal of God's caller as manifest error and denies the refuser any protecting allies.
It sets Satanic bewilderment against companions calling a person back to divine guidance, exposing competing calls and loyalties.
It shows false gods being adopted for honor, a parallel to forming allegiance under a false power.
It contrasts failed evil plotting and severe punishment with honor belonging wholly to God.
It presents the Fire as actively kindled, sharpening the meaning of companions of the blazing fire.
It has the companions of the blazing fire confess that refusing hearing and reason brought them there.
It defines the futility of calling beings that cannot answer, contrasting false summons with a meaningful call.
It is an oath by charging horses and adds no relevant relation.
It adds confession of sin and exclusion from the companions of the blazing fire.
It notes that earlier messengers were denied and that all matters return to God.
It warns that hostile speech can provoke reciprocal abuse, but does not address Satan's party or destination.
It explicitly says Satan calls people toward the blazing fire through inherited following.
It concerns conditions withholding punishment, not Satanic enmity or recruitment.
It describes a caller summoning people to an unprecedented event, without the focus's adversarial relation.
It names the companions of the right, a distinct positive category without a Satanic connection.
It immediately confirms that God seized the disbelievers and asks how His rebuke was.
It links disbelief in God and His messenger to a blazing fire prepared for disbelievers.
It calls disbelievers manifest enemies in a travel-prayer ruling, but not Satan's call or party.
It presents nearer punishment intended to induce return, only broadly related to consequence.
It prohibits allegiance to a people under divine wrath, a distant analogue to hostile affiliation.
It frames hostility to God, His angels, and messengers as reciprocal enmity with God.
It explains that false objects of invocation neither hear nor answer and will repudiate the association.
It concerns the superior resting place of the garden's companions rather than Satan's party.
It completes the Eden deception by recalling that Satan was declared a manifest enemy.
It describes God's eschatological call and response, but not Satan's call to a party.
It excludes devils as the source of revelation, a boundary rather than support for the focus's mechanism.
It calls Moses an enemy and grief to Pharaoh's household in a different narrative setting.
It compares two seas and their benefits, without a relevant enemy or call.
It denies that the familiar companion has gone astray, only distantly echoing the question of guidance.
It combines Satanic derangement with enduring companionship of the Fire for those who persist in usury.
It states that devils are kept from hearing, without adding to the focus relation.
It rejects Satan as the source of the Qur'an, preserving a contrast between divine guidance and Satanic distortion.
It joins a turn from God toward rivals that mislead from His path with becoming companions of the Fire.
It concerns winds, revival of dead land, and resurrection rather than Satanic recruitment.
It warns that rejecting guidance may make a person a patron of Satan.
It shows idolatrous social bonds dissolving into mutual repudiation and Fire, exposing false party solidarity.
It depicts seizure from a near place without an enemy, call, or party relation.
It gives seeking refuge in God as the response when Satan provokes a person.
It explicitly joins devils with a punishment of blazing fire prepared for them.
It notes that those invoked besides God possess nothing, a repeated false-invocation contrast.
It names the companions of the right without contributing to the hostile party or Fire relation.
It describes a future call for destruction, not Satan's calling or companions.
It records Pharaoh's party calling Moses a sorcerer and liar, without a direct focus relation.
It assigns blazing fire to consuming orphans' wealth unjustly, but not through Satanic allegiance.
It describes invocation of what cannot harm or benefit as far error, already covered by stronger call contrasts.
It closes the surah with deferred reckoning at an appointed term, only broadly connected to punishment.
It identifies following every rebellious Satan as a form of uninformed disputation.
It extends the warning about enemies to intimate family relations and commands vigilance.
It concerns God's answer to the distressed caller, a positive invocation pattern outside the focus relation.
It names the companions of the right, with no added relation to Satan or the Fire.
It rejects a false object of call and names the transgressors companions of the Fire.
It praises God as creator and maker of angelic messengers, without a direct enemy or party link.
It provides the contrasting model of God's victorious party through allegiance to God, messenger, and believers.
It calls a false invoked patron and clan bad because its harm is nearer than its benefit.
It records a demand for punishment rather than Satan's enemy relation or his call to a party.
It states that Satan led a person away from the reminder and then abandoned him.
It warns against breaking a strengthened bond for group advantage, only loosely related to party formation.
It shows the Fire's inhabitants calling for release after ignoring their warning, adding the lived outcome of the focus.
It portrays parties dividing and the wrongdoers facing painful punishment.
It contrasts Satan's destination with God's call to the abode of peace and straight path.
It identifies Satanic promptings as something from which the believer seeks God's protection.
It describes prior parties trying to seize their messengers and dispute away truth, but adds no specific Satanic route.
It links denial of the Hour directly to a blazing fire prepared for deniers.
It joins factional partial denial with a call to worship God and return to Him.
It names the companions of the left, a broad adverse counterpart without a direct Satanic link.
It concerns not selling God's covenant for a small price, without the focus's relation.
It directly calls Satan a manifest enemy and forbids following his steps.
It calls a defeated army one of the parties, but lacks the focus's call or Fire destination.
It states that God has prepared a blazing fire for disbelievers, reinforcing the destination after earlier parallels.
It forbids following Satan's steps while commanding wholehearted entry into peace, adding a communal alternative.
It depicts the Fire calling those who turned away, a reversed and less direct call relation.
It contrasts a small rescuing remnant with wrongdoers following luxury and corruption.
It makes opponents who strive to frustrate God's signs companions of the Fire.
It regulates entry to the Prophet's household and social privacy, without relevant support.
It awaits disclosure of who belongs to the straight path, only a distant counterpart to wrong party membership.
It begins Lot's address to his people about indecency, without the focus's enemy or call structure.
It recalls a merciful prior call to God, a positive contrast with limited marginal value.
It connects disbelief and blocking God's path with increased punishment for corruption.
It commands sincere devotion in calling God, contrasting the exclusive divine direction with rival calls.
It shows belief becoming useless after punishment is seen, without adding Satan, party, or blazing-fire detail.
It portrays calling associates besides God as following conjecture rather than knowledge.
It makes Satan cause Adam and his spouse to slip and casts the resulting human condition in terms of mutual enmity.
It specifies Satan's persuasive program: he threatens poverty and commands indecency, against God's promise of forgiveness and bounty.
It attributes believers' momentary setback to Satan exploiting what they had earned.
It says Satan wants those seeking other judgment to go far astray, directly clarifying his aim of diversion.
It explicitly contrasts God's cause with Satan's allies and calls for resisting Satan's party.
It identifies association with false gods as obedience to a rebellious Satan.
It records Satan's own program of leading people astray, filling them with false hopes, and commanding harmful alterations.
It declares Satan's promises and hopes deceptive and gives Hell as the inescapable destination of his followers.
It shows Satan using intoxicants and gambling to sow enmity, hatred, and neglect of God's remembrance and prayer.
It presents devils of humans and jinn as enemies of prophets who inspire deceptive speech to one another.
It depicts devils inspiring their allies to dispute, making obedience to them a form of association.
It warns Adam's children not to let Satan tempt them as he expelled their parents and identifies devils as allies of disbelievers.
It explains misguidance through taking devils as allies instead of God while imagining oneself guided.
It shows one who abandons divine signs being followed and overcome by Satan.
It portrays Satan making evil deeds attractive, promising support, and then abandoning his party when confrontation arrives.
It directly calls Satan a manifest enemy to humanity while warning of his plotting.
It has Satan admit that he only called and people responded, deny coercive authority, and leave his followers responsible for their choice.
It records Satan's vow to make wrongdoing attractive and to mislead people broadly.
It limits Satan's authority by excluding God's sincere servants from his power.
It names Hell as the promised gathering place for Satan's followers.
It states that Satan made former peoples' deeds attractive, became their patron, and is linked to painful punishment.
It confines Satan's authority to those who take him as patron and associate partners with God.
It calls squanderers brothers of devils, showing how conduct can establish a Satanic kinship.
It details Satan's means of recruitment through voice, mobilized forces, wealth, children, and deceptive promises.
It commands Abraham's father not to serve Satan because Satan is rebellious against the Most Merciful.
It identifies Satan's whisper to Adam as the lure of permanence and an unending dominion.
It warns believers not to follow Satan's steps because he commands indecency and wrongdoing.
It attributes a people's blocked path to Satan making their deeds attractive, preventing guidance.
It says Satan beautified former peoples' deeds and barred them from the path despite their discernment.
It states that Satan led a great multitude astray, demonstrating the scale of the party he gathers.
It describes a devil assigned as a close companion to one who turns from God's remembrance.
It says such companions bar people from the path while the misled think themselves guided.
It shows the final repudiation of the evil companion and the distance between follower and Satanic companion.
It attributes apostasy after guidance to Satan making it attractive and extending false hopes.
It identifies the retreating whisperer as a continuing source of inward suggestion.
It locates the whisperer's activity in the hearts of people.
It extends the whispering threat across both jinn and human agents.
